title: Baked Ziti
subtitle: penne in a beefy tomato sauce layered with creamy ricotta and baked under bubbling mozzarella
imageAlt: A 9×13 dish of baked pasta with browned bubbling mozzarella, one scoop taken out, on a navy napkin
servingsNote: a 9×13 pan: dinner for two, plus 4 lunches

breakdown: Onion, garlic, dried Italian seasoning, salt, pepper

beforeYouStart.text: Undercook the pasta by 2 minutes; it finishes in the oven.
Oven at 190°C (375°F), with a greased 9×13 baking dish.

steps.title: Boil the pasta
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Cook the penne in a large pot of boiling salted water 2 minutes less than the package says, and drain.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Meanwhile, brown the beef and onion in a large deep skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, 8–10 minutes until no pink remains and it reads 71°C (160°F). Spoon off the fat and add the garlic for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Stir in the marinara, tomato sauce, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper and simmer 5 minutes.

steps.title: Ricotta mix
steps.text: Stir the ricotta, egg and ¼ cup of the Parmesan together in a bowl.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Toss the pasta with the meat sauce. Spread half in a 9×13-inch (23×33 cm) baking dish, dot with the ricotta mixture and sprinkle with 1 cup of the mozzarella. Top with the rest of the pasta, then the remaining 1½ cups mozzarella and ¼ cup Parmesan.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Cover with foil and bake 20 minutes. Uncover and bake 15 minutes more, until the cheese is bubbling and browned at the edges and the centre reads 74°C (165°F). Rest 10 minutes.

fixIt.fix: The pasta was fully cooked first and soaked up the sauce. Undercook it by 2 minutes, and keep it covered for the first 20.
Drain the ricotta if it's wet, and let the dish rest the full 10 minutes.
Broil 2–3 minutes at the end, watching closely.

saleTip: Lean ground beef is often $4.40/lb on sale; buy the family pack and freeze 450 g portions flat in bags.
swap: Ground turkey: same amount, cooked to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Reheat squares covered; they're great for lunches all week.
doneness: Ground beef cooked to 71°C (160°F) with no pink (Health Canada); the baked dish bubbling at the edges and steaming hot in the centre.
source: Based on tested baked ziti methods (Canadian Living, Food Network Canada): undercooked pasta tossed in meat sauce, layered with a ricotta-egg mix and mozzarella, baked covered then uncovered at 190°C (375°F).
prepAhead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead, cover and refrigerate. Bake covered 35 minutes, then uncovered 15.
reheat: Covered with foil at 180°C (350°F) 20–25 minutes, or single portions in the microwave 2–3 minutes, until steaming hot, 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: A meatless baked ziti with sauce, ricotta and mozzarella.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the beef and onion; put the garlic straight into the sauce in the next step.

fancy.note: Mild Italian sausage instead of beef, and a crispy Parmesan top.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: brown the sausage meat the same way, to 71°C (160°F) with no pink.
stepNotes.5: Fancy: scatter the extra Parmesan over the top before it goes back in uncovered.

plating: Lift out with a wide spatula so the layers show.

why.2-1: The egg sets the ricotta so it stays creamy in layers instead of running.
why.1-4: The extra tomato sauce keeps the pasta saucy after baking.

funFact: Baked ziti is an Italian-American Sunday classic; ziti are long tubes in Italy, but penne is the easy swap here.

keeps.note: freeze baked portions or the whole unbaked dish, wrapped well
